clue.text: Empty tank container to be loaded

indicators.note: a tank that is loaded has something put inside it, so the container goes into the tank

parts.note: a vat is a large tank for liquids
a can is a metal container

explanation.surface: A soldier or driver notes an empty tank waiting to be filled from a container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty tank' reads as one phrase, but 'Empty' is the definition and 'tank' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an unoccupied room or seat is described as empty or not in use.

clue.text: Love a party with endless wine

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the word for wine is cut off

parts.note: red is a type of wine

explanation.surface: Someone's idea of love: a party where the wine never runs out.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to love someone deeply is to worship or cherish them.

clue.text: Take it in turns to change a net at sea

parts.note: to alter is to change

indicators.note: at sea means confused or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fishermen agree to take turns rearranging a net while out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' turns A NET into NATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: people who swap a duty back and forth between them each act in their turn.

clue.text: Excellent spinner following advice

indicators.note: following says the spinner word comes after the advice word

parts.note: a tip is a piece of advice
a top is a toy that spins

explanation.surface: A cricket coach praises a spin bowler who followed the advice given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinner' suggests a cricket bowler; here it is a child's spinning toy.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: first-rate or of the very highest quality, an informal word of praise.

clue.text: Curiosity at home about bisecting experiment

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: bisecting means cutting in two, so the word for about splits the word for experiment

parts.note: a test is an experiment
re is Latin-derived for about or concerning

explanation.surface: A scientist at home is curious about cutting a trial in half.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a wish to know more about something; showing it means being curious.

clue.text: Trendy school, limited in scope

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy
a comprehensive is a British state secondary school taking pupils of all abilities

explanation.surface: A critic sneers that a fashionable school offers only a narrow education.
explanation.walkthrough: A comprehensive is the standard British state secondary school, open to all abilities.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposite of all-embracing: something narrow in coverage fails to take everything in.

clue.text: One developing ideas in article on various riots

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the article comes first

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: various means differing or assorted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer on politics develops ideas in an article about various riots.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: someone who forms and develops hypotheses or abstract explanations.

clue.text: Bird's bill, gold colour on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: a nib is a bird's beak or bill
or is the heraldic name for gold

explanation.surface: A bird's beak shows a golden colour when seen in a mirror.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's means 'is'; 'on reflection' reverses NIB + OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a familiar red-breasted garden songbird.

clue.text: Head wearing sample timing device

indicators.note: something wearing a garment has it around it, so the word for sample goes around the word for head

parts.note: a swatch is a sample of fabric
top means head, as in the top of a page

explanation.surface: A head is draped in a fabric sample, with a timer nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a handheld watch started and halted to measure elapsed time exactly.

clue.text: Fine actor, he cracked up describing the old man in an old western

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: describing here means drawing a line around, so the anagram goes around the father
cracked up means broken apart, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father, the old man

explanation.surface: A fine actor broke down while describing his father in an old cowboy film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracked up' turns ACTOR HE into ORTACHE; 'describing' puts PA inside it after F.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a 1948 John Ford cavalry film starring John Wayne and Henry Fonda.

clue.text: Perhaps an annual charge

definitions.meaning: an annual is a yearly published volume, one kind of bound volume
police charge a suspect when they enter an offence formally in the records

explanation.surface: Is that an annual fee being levied?
explanation.walkthrough: 'annual charge' looks like a yearly fee; split it, and an annual is a yearly volume while 'charge' is the police sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's annual is a yearly volume; police formally record an offence against a suspect.

clue.text: Item handed down from extremely humble Irish weaver?

indicators.note: extremely means the extreme letters, the first and last, of the following word

parts.note: a loom weaves cloth, so it is a weaver of sorts; the question mark flags the stretch

explanation.surface: A treasured item handed down from a very humble Irish weaver.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a valued possession passed from one generation of a family to the next.

clue.text: Fame achieved by some in theatre, now nobodies

indicators.note: some in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some once-famous stage actors are now nobodies.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the celebrity or wide acclaim someone has won.

clue.text: Drop a series of novels involving a family's history

definitions.text: series of novels involving a family's history

parts.note: to sag is to droop or drop

explanation.surface: A reader's interest drops during a long run of family-history novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a long chronicle, often in several volumes, following generations of one family.

clue.text: Get better workers in a time leading to change

indicators.note: in says the first pair of words goes inside the letters of a and time

parts.note: to mend is to recover or get better
men are workers, as in a firm's staff

explanation.surface: Workers want improvement soon, leading to reform.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a formal alteration, as to a law or motion.

clue.text: Firm that's manufactured our steel

indicators.note: manufactured means made or put together, so the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: An advertisement for a steelworks: the company that made our steel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company noun; it is an adjective meaning determined.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: unwavering and determined in purpose.

clue.text: A shop, alas, mistreated dog

indicators.note: mistreated means handled badly, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A pet shop, sadly, has mistreated a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small long-haired breed from Tibet.

clue.text: Telegram about case confused smart alec

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for telegram goes around the anagram

parts.note: a wire is an old word for a telegram

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A telegram about a muddled legal case baffles a know-all.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a know-all who pretends to wisdom he lacks.

clue.text: Always swallowed by swimmer with a temperature

indicators.note: swallowed by means taken inside, so the word for always goes within the word for swimmer

parts.note: a fish is a swimmer
ever means always

explanation.surface: Someone always swallowed by a swimmer would surely run a fever.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: suffering a fever, so running a high body heat.

clue.text: Expert nursing husband in pain

indicators.note: nursing means holding or cradling, so the expert holds the husband inside

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: An expert nurse tends a husband who is in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a dull continuous hurt.

clue.text: Busy, even at university!

parts.note: tied means level or even, as in a scoreline
up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A student exclaims that even at university life is busy.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: occupied and unable to attend to anything else.

clue.text: This being fit to eat, the Spanish stay over

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
to bide is to stay or wait

explanation.surface: A traveller judges a meal fit to eat and decides to stay longer in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: safe or suitable to be consumed as food.

clue.text: Flowering shrub shown in British volume

parts.note: room means space or volume, as in room to spare

explanation.surface: A flowering shrub is pictured in a British book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'volume' suggests a book; here it means space.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a yellow-flowered shrub of heath and hillside.

clue.text: Pest is lying in shade

indicators.note: lying in means resting inside, so the word is goes within the word for shade

parts.note: a nuance is a shade of meaning or colour

explanation.surface: A pest is lying in the shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an annoying person or thing.

clue.text: Constant speed in decrepit car

parts.note: C is the scientific symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
rate means speed

explanation.surface: An old banger can only manage a steady speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: an informal word for an old, rundown vehicle.

clue.text: That woman, old champion

parts.note: her refers to that woman

explanation.surface: That woman used to be a champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone admired as a winner or courageous figure.

clue.text: Easy thing to do in 'Peter Pan', say

definitions.meaning: something no harder than a task for a youngster
Peter Pan is a stage drama written for young audiences

explanation.surface: Acting in Peter Pan is supposedly a doddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for a simple task; and literally a drama meant for youngsters, as Barrie's Peter Pan is.

clue.text: Charge impressed English

parts.note: stamped means impressed, as a mark pressed into a surface

explanation.surface: An Englishman was impressed by a charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impressed' means marked by pressure, not admiring.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a sudden headlong rush of animals or people.

clue.text: Wading bird quietly settled across lake

indicators.note: across means spanning, so the other letters stretch around the lake

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly
over means finished or settled

explanation.surface: A wading bird quietly settles down across a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a short-billed bird of shores and wetlands, such as the lapwing.
